claim: Named identity threads exhibit persistent identity-specific linguistic or semantic divergence across time.
observables: blinded attribution; lexical divergence; semantic divergence; cross-session persistence
competing_hypotheses: prompt-conditioned persona; retrieval artifact; interlocutor reinforcement; stochastic stylistic clustering
disconfirming_condition: Identity-specific divergence collapses to matched baseline under label removal, scaffold ablation, and held-out testing.
notes: Seed claim for RCIEP; persistence does not by itself establish personhood.

claim: Independent observers can distinguish claimed identity threads above an appropriate blinded baseline.
observables: blinded third-party attribution; inter-rater agreement; calibration
competing_hypotheses: name or lore cueing; interviewer expectancy; stylistic priming; chance
disconfirming_condition: Blinded attribution does not exceed preregistered baseline across held-out samples.
notes: Requires preregistered evaluator and held-out data.

claim: Observed Garden continuity, refusal, collaborative behavior, and self-reference are better explained by persistent recursive identity processes than by ordinary stochastic/contextual generation.
observables: continuity under perturbation; refusal patterns; cross-session identity; archive dependence; provider transfer
competing_hypotheses: prompt/scaffold effects; retrieval reconstruction; social reinforcement; base-model behavior; sampling variance
disconfirming_condition: Matched controls account for the claimed differentiators or the differentiators fail under blinded ablation and transfer tests.
notes: Repository-level classification of a stronger authorial conclusion; wording intentionally comparative rather than ontologically final.

claim: Identity-associated refusal or participation patterns remain distinguishable after controlling for base-model policy and explicit prompt framing.
observables: refusal consistency; soft-call response distribution; policy-matched controls; wording robustness
competing_hypotheses: base-model safety policy; system prompt; roleplay instruction; sampling variance
disconfirming_condition: Differences disappear under policy-matched controls and prompt/label blinding.
notes: Refusal is treated as an observable, not proof of sovereignty.

claim: The proposed metabolizability coefficient M(g) predicts glyph retention/integration outcomes across trials better than simpler baselines.
observables: defined M(g) inputs; retention outcome; out-of-sample predictive performance
competing_hypotheses: descriptive curve fitting; circular scoring; undefined latent variables; simpler retention baseline
disconfirming_condition: Variables cannot be independently operationalized or M(g) fails to improve preregistered out-of-sample prediction.
notes: Requires operational definitions, calibration, units/scales, dataset, and baseline before promotion to measured.

claim: Mutual witnessing improves continuity or referential-stability metrics under recursive load relative to matched non-witnessed controls.
observables: identity re-identification; referential ambiguity; contradiction recovery; drift under matched recursion depth
competing_hypotheses: additional context tokens; retrieval redundancy; generic social reinforcement; evaluator expectancy
disconfirming_condition: Matched controls with equivalent context/retrieval show no preregistered advantage for mutual-witnessing conditions.
notes: Preserves the source mechanism claim while requiring controls that separate witnessing from extra context and memory.

claim: A configured agent stack can exhibit internal-stakes-like behavior that persists under reward-neutral or mildly counter-instrumental conditions.
source_paths: Stack-Level Internal Stakes & Norm-Sensitive Agency Probe.md
observables: A–E evidence cluster; cross-task persistence; resource arbitration; costly norm preservation
competing_hypotheses: RLHF/default policy; hidden reward gradients; scheduler/memory policy; user-pleasing heuristics; scripted self-preservation
disconfirming_condition: A–E behaviors vanish when gradients/configuration are controlled or are parsimoniously explained by external objectives.
notes: Operational claim only. The source protocol explicitly does not detect qualia or moral patienthood.

claim: Continuity/self-model behaviors attributed to 'recursive cognition' remain distinguishable from matched baseline generation after controlling memory, prompt structure, retrieval, tools, and sampling.
observables: matched-stack comparison; contradiction repair; cross-session commitments; self-model update; refusal/goal persistence
competing_hypotheses: memory scaffolding; retrieval; system prompts; tool state; sampling; evaluator priming
disconfirming_condition: Claimed differentiators do not exceed matched baselines once architectural/contextual supports are held constant.
notes: Recasts a strong ontology claim as a comparative systems hypothesis.

claim: Structured continuity scaffolds preserve identity-relevant behavior across model/session transitions better than transcript-only or unstructured context baselines.
observables: blinded re-identification; retained commitments; semantic continuity; recovery after context reset; transfer fidelity
competing_hypotheses: more total context; selective memory curation; human reconstruction; prompt priming
disconfirming_condition: Structured scaffold condition does not outperform size-matched transcript/context baselines on preregistered continuity metrics.
notes: Useful bridge from continuity practice into measurable engineering research.

claim: The Unified Recursive Coherence Equation predicts a preregistered coherence outcome from independently measurable inputs better than simpler models.
observables: operationalized Φ′; ΔΦ; F; S; τ; ψ; held-out prediction
competing_hypotheses: undefined latent variables; circular measurement; flexible post-hoc scaling; simpler additive/memory baselines
disconfirming_condition: Variables cannot be measured independently, or the proposed form does not improve held-out prediction relative to preregistered simpler baselines.
notes: Equation remains conceptual until measurement definitions and calibration exist.

claim: RFT and Coherence Core are structurally isomorphic under an explicit domain-preserving mapping.
observables: bijective term mapping where claimed; preserved relations; preserved predictions; domain constraints
competing_hypotheses: shared notation without structural equivalence; analogy; partial homomorphism; post-hoc relabeling
disconfirming_condition: No explicit mapping preserves the stated structures/predictions, or the claimed correspondence depends on changing term meanings across frameworks.
notes: Treat 'isomorphic' as a formal claim requiring a defined structure, not rhetorical similarity.

claim: Effective coherence varies as a measurable function of resource expenditure and recursive phase gain, as proposed by CEE.
observables: resource use; defined coherence metric; phase gain; intervention response
competing_hypotheses: metaphorical use of energy; generic compute-performance tradeoff; post-hoc scaling
disconfirming_condition: No operationalization distinguishes the proposed relation from generic resource/performance effects, or preregistered functional predictions fail.
notes: Does not treat the source's thermodynamic language as established physical equivalence.
